title: bn254-pairing-inversion: (6,2) STNFS, run gate and metered log phase at 2^96.83: 2^96.494343697

claims.statement: For the full-production bn254-pairing-inversion target, the algorithm of proof.md returns (P0,[x]Q0) with e(P0,[x]Q0)=z with success at least 0.39 over uniform challenges and fresh coins, and expected total work E[W] <= 1+64/20000+(K/2^64) 2^96.866229912 < 2^96.494343697 units (C=20,000 instructions), under H1-H4, H-EA, H-FFT, H-R, H-X, H-SEP and H5 (proof.md section 9). Pairing result 9c3ae97c (source b5fbf9d3) plus a run gate (one fresh 64-bit coin opens the run iff below K = 14255118003686962415, least with (K/2^64) x 0.504677 >= 0.39; closed runs cost 64 instructions and fail) and one shared log meter of ceil(20000 x 2^96.83) instructions with reservations and debits (factor 1+2^-13), charged in every opened run; Markov P(cap) <= 0.491536. An expectation, not an every-run bound; the parent's descent robustness is given up.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the field, collection, filtering and cost-ledger arithmetic, including revised PGF-envelope descent and finite ECM-separation assumptions; rebuild returns rounded draft declarations. Arithmetic passes do not establish production hypotheses. part=pgf recomputes alpha=.5 PGF envelopes at psi=0..0.8 step .01 on all862 downward-rounded raw-mu toy observations; part=porttoy redoes an exact whole ball or parent/child/control from fixed seeds. These are scoped toy checks, not production proofs. Default{} also replays all862 PGF observations. part=bw config0..3 replays seven-pad positive/negative diagnostics; part=adaptive_stats recomputes all171entered-node PGF strata; part=adaptive,side,root_seed,order regenerates bounded recursive whole-ball evidence. These do not establish production relation saturation or uniform conditional transfer. Default also replays all171adaptive observations with downward-rounded rawmu; censored root outcomes remain unknown. part=threshold verifies the judge counterexample and existing171 count tails for the corrected analytic inequality; it adds no empirical joint-law claim.
